name: window.move
description: Move and/or resize a window by handle. Optionally bring it to the foreground in the same atomic call (avoids the focus-race window between move + window.focus).

handle.description: Window handle from window.list, e.g. 'win:0x1A2B' or 'mac:42'.

x.description: New x position in virtual-screen coordinates.

y.description: New y position in virtual-screen coordinates.

w.description: New width in pixels. If omitted, width is preserved.

h.description: New height in pixels. If omitted, height is preserved.

foreground.description: Also bring the window to the foreground after the move. Foreground attempt is reported separately in `foreground_status` (it may fail with `lock_held` while the move succeeds). See issue #73.

bounds.description: Final window bounds after the move (post-clamping by the OS / monitor edges).

prior_bounds.description: Window bounds before the move. Symmetric with `window.focus.prior_handle` — caller can use this to restore later.

foreground_status.description: Outcome of the foreground attempt. `not_requested` when `foreground` was false; `ok` on success; `lock_held` when foreground-lock denied the focus change (move still succeeded). See issue #73.

x-implementations.name: set_window_pos
x-implementations.description: Win32 `GetWindowRect` (capture prior_bounds) + `SetWindowPos(hwnd, HWND_TOP, x, y, w, h, flags)`. When `w`/`h` are omitted, SWP_NOSIZE is set. When `foreground: true`, follow with `SetForegroundWindow` and capture its return value as `foreground_status`.

x-implementations.name: move_window
x-implementations.description: Win32 `MoveWindow` legacy alternative — same effect; less flag granularity.

windows-modern.description: SetWindowPos / MoveWindow against the supplied handle. UIPI may reject moves against higher-IL windows — returns ERR uipi_blocked. Foreground attempt subject to foreground-lock; failure returns foreground_status: lock_held with the move's effects intact.

windows-classic.description: Same Win32 APIs (available since NT 3.1). No UIPI, so cross-process moves are not blocked at the kernel boundary. NT 4 has no foreground-lock; foreground_status is always `ok` or `not_requested` on NT 4. NT 5+ may return `lock_held`.
